title.narrative: Provision of essential cooperation and information services on safety, security, and access to humanitarian aid organizations in Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtThe main purpose of the project is to assist NGOs in delivering aid safely through the provision of essential security coordination and information services that help them understand the operating environment and reduce the risks facing their staff and operations. INSO has been operating in Somalia since 2015. The underlying principle in INSO’s theory of change is that better and more accurate security information leads to better decisions. IF NGOs working in Somalia assisting conflict and disaster-affected populations have access to INSO safety and security services, THEN they would be able to have enhanced access to the vulnerable population BECAUSE NGOs will have better information on which to base decisions at tactical, operational, and strategic levels while delivering assistance. ltbrgtINSO runs a single project that is co-funded by 5 donors (including SHF) and all donors contribute to the realization of the project’s objectives and attainment of deliverables. INSO was impacted by the USAID/BHA funding cuts, with a cessation of program directive received in February 2025, effectively terminating an ongoing 24-month $1.9 million grant (August 2024 to July 2026). Sustained and increased support from existing donors is essential to maintaining core INSO services for the NGO community in Somalia. ltbrgtGiven the evolving security environment and the emerging uncertainties related to the AUSSOM transition, resurgent AS and a major political transition that is testing a fragile political pact, the Somalia operating context is getting even more complex, with varying layers of protracted armed conflict and acute/emerging contestation between multiple actors. NGOs face strong challenges related to access and security, including inadequate capacity to understand the dynamic context, difficulty in accessing and verifying information, lack of information sharing, lack of security coordination and harmonized security practices, poor security awareness of staff, and lack of training opportunities. ltbrgtTo address the needs/gaps mentioned above, INSO’s services comprising a Conflict and Humanitarian Data Centre (CHDC)—a secure cloud-based database containing all security incidents occurring in Somalia with integrated visualization and GIS tools—flash alert reporting, scheduled analytical reporting and briefings, field-based NGO security roundtables, individual security advisories, training, and crisis management assistance — play an important role in establishing a baseline of credible information, delivering usable analysis on which to base programming and risk management decisions, and furnishing the skills and tools required to navigate the environment and deliver aid safely. This in turn promotes NGOs’ delivery of services to their beneficiaries and the fulfilment of their projects and programs. With the new funding cycle, INSO will continue its field presence and ensure greater responsiveness to NGO needs at a time where funding cuts and an evolving context continue to complicate access, and reduce NGO capacities. INSO’s activities currently benefit 177 NGOs, 7 UN agencies, and 6 Humanitarian Donor Agencies..
